scope_checks.result: Explicitly absent. Intermediate-support parity has 4k gates and distance N/2 from every center for m>=2k+2; it is a missed YES table at large lengths.
Under the stated inner budget inequality, every accepted table belongs to YES, hence no NO or gap table is accepted.
For each fixed beta in (0,1/3), k=beta*m-2log2(m)+O(1), t=Theta(N^beta/m^2); no beta(m) tending to zero is substituted.
For any epsilon>0 choose beta_0 with H(beta)<epsilon below beta_0. For each such fixed beta, the exact gate upper bound is eventually below N^(1+epsilon).
The sufficient condition is distance>2t+1, not just >2t. Centers 000 and 111 at t=1 are an explicit endpoint counterexample.
Full-parity shifts change the coarse lower bound to N/2, not N. The max(1,2k) exponent handles this.
Counts reachable outgoing wire slots, including parallel uses. The bound is representation-specific and is not a minimum-reuse or minimum-formula lower bound.
Every population counter, comparison, parity input negation and OR gate is expanded into the declared ordinary basis; center functions are not enumerated by the recognizer.
Coordinate subcubes, not NP witnesses or arbitrary fibers of decoded gate values. Initial-restriction overlap uses the Phase 2 definition unchanged.

General separated-tube geometry and ordinary-junta distance are Lean theorems. Shifted cross-family balance, compiler correctness for all sizes and fixed-beta asymptotics have explicit manual proofs plus bounded tests.
Small atlas and giant integer parameter examples are controls only. Huge circuits are never constructed or claimed exhaustively checked.
